title: UK AISI Inspect Platform: Model Evaluation Standards - August 2026 Release
context: 2026-08-28 engine cycle - UK AI Safety Institute released Inspect v2 evaluation framework August 2026; mandatory for frontier model developers accessing UK government compute and procurement gates
body: The UK AI Safety Institute Inspect platform, released in its v2 iteration August 2026, provides a standardised evaluation harness for frontier AI models. It operationalises the UK AI Regulation Bill requirement for independent pre-deployment safety evaluation by defining a set of capability and safety benchmarks that models must pass before they can access UK government procurement gates or compute allocations. The platform evaluates across four axes: capability - raw performance on reasoning, coding, and knowledge benchmarks; safety - resistance to jailbreak, prompt injection, and harmful instruction following; alignment - measured divergence between stated model policy and observed behaviour under adversarial sampling; containment - boundary-enforcement fidelity under iterative red-teaming. The Council of AI reads the AISI Inspect platform as a measurement infrastructure play: the value is not the benchmark scores themselves but the reproducibility and verifiability of the evaluation pipeline. A model developer who runs Inspect on their own hardware produces a self-assessment; the same model run through Inspect on AISI-controlled infrastructure with signed output produces a verified measurement credential. The posture is monitored containment, not provable isolation - Inspect does not certify a model as safe, it certifies that a specific evaluation was conducted under specified conditions and that the resulting boundary measurements are independently verifiable. Concretely: frontier developers targeting UK public-sector deployment should run Inspect v2 with CSOAI-signed output capture; the signed evaluation record feeds the Containment Incident Index, so post-deployment divergence from the pre-deployment baseline triggers a containment boundary event; the verified measurement credential from Inspect is cross-jurisdiction portable - equivalent frameworks under the EU AI Act Article 15 accuracy obligations and US OMB M-24-10 accept the signed evaluation record as evidence.
